text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--Danish competitiveness on world markets has slipped to 20th place from last year's 11th on an index compiled by the World Economic Forum.
--A parliamentary majority is expected on Wednesday to vote against a centre-right initiative to remove a levy on owner-occupiers.
--BG Bank is expected to announce an alliance with the Danish post office by the end of this week.
--An EU push to remove internal borders is likely to oblige Denmark to hold a new referendum.

--Six consortia have applied for new oil and gas exploration concessions in the Danish North Sea. The Danish Energy Agency declines to give details of the groupings, but among bidders are Amaranda Hess, Statoil, A.P. Moeller, Shell, Mobil, Agip and Phillips Petroleum.
--Denmark will follow a hard line to preserve its four EU opt-outs and stay outside any supranational asylum policy, says Justice Minister Frank Jensen.
--Danish furniture exports rose by nine percent in the first two months of 1997.
--Local authorities will have to find an extra 5.35 billion crowns in 1998 if they want to maintain services at the present level. REUTER
